about.label: About
about.p1: Over eight years I've moved between software development, e-commerce and growth experimentation, and the mix stuck: I can architect a clean Shopify theme, design an A/B test that holds up statistically, and read what it did to the business, all in the same sprint.
about.p2: Right now my focus is Shopify OS 2.0 performance, CRO strategy and revenue optimization. The experimentation programs I've led land 20-30% uplifts on the tests that win. Along the way I managed two developers and built 20+ internal tools that took the place of expensive vendor software.
about.p3: I work best in small, fast teams where speed, data and business outcomes matter more than process for its own sake. Ambiguity doesn't bother me, I'm fluent in English, and I'm used to working across time zones.

impact.label: Impact
impact.headline: Where the code moved revenue
impact.intro: Every entry here starts with a problem, says what I did about it, and ends with the number it moved. These are the points where a technical decision showed up in a business metric.

highlights.title: Conversion Rate from 0.5% to 1.2%
highlights.context: The store had traffic and was losing it at the door. Friction sat in three places (product page, cart drawer, checkout) and none of them had ever been instrumented or tested in any systematic way.
highlights.actions: I went through the whole purchase path with session data and heatmaps, then picked the points worth attacking first. Rebuilt the cart flow, redesigned the trust signals on the product page, and set up a testing cadence in Intelligems that ran 4+ experiments a week to significance.
highlights.impact: CVR went from 0.5% to 1.2%, a 140% improvement. Winning tests landed in the 20-30% range. At that traffic volume, every point of CVR was real incremental revenue with no extra ad spend.

highlights.title: Shopify Theme Overhaul: Performance That Converts
highlights.context: The store ran on a legacy theme carrying years of app installs. LCP was slow, the UX had drifted apart template by template, and both SEO and conversion were paying for it.
highlights.actions: Rebuilt the theme from scratch on Shopify OS 2.0. Dropped the redundant third-party apps and rewrote what they did as small Liquid and JavaScript components. Restructured the homepage, product pages and cart. Optimized images, deferred the non-critical scripts, and added lazy loading on every high-traffic template.
highlights.impact: Core Web Vitals improved across the board and page load came down. The apps we removed came off the monthly bill. And with a cleaner theme, shipping the next change stopped being an archaeology exercise.

highlights.title: 20+ Internal Tools That Replaced Vendor Software
highlights.context: The team leaned on expensive, rigid SaaS tools. Each one added a step to a workflow, and together they made iterating on an A/B test slow and costly.
highlights.actions: Went through the tool stack looking for what could be automated, then built the replacements: 20+ internal tools and scripts, from data pipelines that pulled Shopify analytics into dashboards to reporting jobs that killed the manual weekly export.
highlights.impact: Less vendor software to pay for, and that budget went back into the team. Experiments moved faster once the reporting bottleneck was gone. Within a quarter the team was iterating at twice the pace.

highlights.title: 4+ Experiments Per Week at Statistical Significance
highlights.context: Most e-commerce CRO programs run one or two tests a month, which is not enough to learn anything quickly. The goal was a setup that could run, read and ship winners fast enough to matter.
highlights.actions: Built a lean framework around it: hypotheses prioritized with ICE scoring, variants prototyped fast with AI assistance, setup and QA in Intelligems, and a decision protocol after each test so nothing kept running past significance.
highlights.impact: 4+ experiments a week, sustained, all reaching significance. That was the fastest the team had ever learned. Winners came in at 20-30%. Quarter over quarter, the compounding showed up in revenue.

highlights.title: Engineering Team Leadership: Delivery Without Bloat
highlights.context: Two junior developers joined with no delivery process and uneven output. The task was to raise their velocity and their ownership without burying anyone in ceremony.
highlights.actions: Put in a light Agile cadence: tickets scoped clearly, async standups, peer review on every PR, a retro each week. Added AI-assisted tooling to speed up their day, and made it clear who owned what and what counted as done.
highlights.impact: Delivery speed went up and stayed up. Code quality improved once review became routine. Both developers took on wider scope within six months, and onboarding them cost the team no velocity.

highlights.title: ERP Module Development: Large-Scale Production Systems
highlights.context: A corporate ERP serving enterprise clients needed new modules, and the systems it ran on could not go down while we added them.
highlights.actions: Built several production ERP modules with ExtJS on the front end and Laravel behind it. Designed and tuned the MySQL queries that had to work over large tables. Deployments were zero-downtime, and I handled the server-side problems when they came up.
highlights.impact: Modules landed on schedule with no critical incidents in production. Report generation got noticeably faster after the query work. The systems stayed up for the whole engagement.

projects.label: Projects
projects.headline: Selected Projects.
projects.headlineSub: Systems I built to replace vendor software, with the numbers that came out of them.

items.title: Custom Email Capture Popup: 52% More Subscribers Than Alia
items.summary: Replaced Alia, a paid Shopify capture app, with a popup built in JavaScript and Liquid and embedded in the theme itself. No external dependencies.
items.context: The store used Alia, a paid third-party app, to collect email subscribers through popups. It worked, but changing copy, design or triggers meant working around whatever the app allowed. Every iteration was a negotiation with someone else's product.
items.actions: Built the popup from scratch in JavaScript and Liquid, straight into the Shopify theme. Timing, scroll triggers, mobile-first layout, and copy anyone on the team could edit. With no app layer in the middle, a change went live the same day.
items.impact: Weekly signups went from 250 with Alia to 380 with the custom build, up 52%, and the monthly app fee disappeared. Owning the whole thing meant we could keep improving it instead of filing feature requests.

items.title: Real-Time Inventory Sync: Shopify ↔ Amazon ↔ Mercado Libre
items.summary: A custom sync that keeps stock consistent across Shopify, Amazon and Mercado Libre in real time. No more overselling and no more manual updates across 6,000 SKUs and 5,000 orders a month.
items.context: The store sold on three channels at once (Shopify, Amazon, Mercado Libre) and inventory was handled by hand. Every order on one channel meant somebody updating the other two. Overselling was a permanent risk: sell out on Amazon and the other two would happily keep taking orders. The operational cost was real, and so was the margin for error.
items.actions: Designed and built a two-way sync engine in TypeScript and Node.js. Shopify webhooks fire on every order, fulfillment and manual stock adjustment, including bulk edits through Matrixify, and push the change straight to Amazon (SP-API) and Mercado Libre (their official API). Going the other way, a polling service runs every 5 minutes to pull order and stock changes from both marketplaces back into Shopify. Conflict resolution, retry logic and error logging are in there so nothing gets dropped quietly.
items.impact: 6,000 SKUs stay in sync across 3 channels with nobody touching them. 5,000 orders a month go through automatically and the overselling stopped. Shopify to marketplace is instant; marketplace back to Shopify lands inside 5 minutes. Operations dropped the manual inventory routine entirely.

items.title: Custom Search Engine: Algolia Replacement Built In-House
items.summary: A full search engine built into the Shopify theme to replace Algolia: synonyms, autocomplete, word prediction, better relevance ranking and recent searches. Licensing cost of zero.
items.context: The store paid for Algolia to run its search. It was capable, but between the cost, the integration overhead and how little control we had over ranking logic, it was worth trying to replace. The goal was an equivalent experience we could change whenever we wanted.
items.actions: Built the engine in TypeScript and JavaScript, embedded in the theme through Liquid. It indexes product data and handles fuzzy matching and synonyms for typo-tolerant queries, predictive autocomplete as you type, word prediction for likely completions, relevance ranking based on product metadata, and a recent-searches history kept client-side. No third-party search service anywhere in it.
items.impact: It's running as an A/B test against Algolia in production right now. So far it performs on par on the search engagement metrics, with the added benefit of full ownership, no licensing fee, and ranking logic I can change without waiting on a vendor. The test is still going; I'll publish numbers once it reaches significance.

items.title: Dignemi: Mental Wellness App for Spanish Speakers
items.summary: A privacy-first, offline-first mental health app for the Spanish-speaking market. People track how they're doing, run guided exercises and keep a diary, with no connection required and nothing leaving the phone unless they say so.
items.context: Mental health apps for the Hispanic market tend to be in English, careless with privacy, or useless without a connection. Dignemi was built the other way round: analytics off by default, cloud sync only if you opt in, and everything stored on the device until the user decides otherwise.
items.actions: TypeScript end to end. On the front, React Native 0.81.5 with Expo SDK 54, Expo Router 6 for typed file-based navigation, Zustand for session and preference state, and SQLite (expo-sqlite) for local persistence under an offline-first sync model. On the back, a NestJS REST API on Render with JWT auth, server-side Google Sign-In validation, and an incremental two-way sync engine (push/pull with deviceUpdatedAt, isDeleted and synced flags). Four validated psychological assessments are in there (GAD-2, GAD-7, PHQ-2, PSS-4) with the full intro → questions → result → recommendation flow. Plus an animated breathing player with configurable protocols, a multi-step guided exercise system, an emotional diary with mood tracking and tags, a content library, and structured multi-session programs. Animations use React Native Reanimated 4 with staggered patterns and spring physics. New Architecture and React Compiler are on experimentally. The design system is my own: semantic palette, type scale, spacing, shadows, radii and motion tokens in one theme file.
items.impact: Nearly finished. It covers full-stack TypeScript, offline-first data design, privacy by default, a fair amount of animation work, and enough mental health UX to be useful. Built because the gap in Spanish-language mental health apps is a real one.

items.title: Custom Rebuy Replacement: Unified Recommendation Engine for Shopify
items.summary: A custom recommendation widget system built to replace Rebuy: 6 widget types across 5 page templates, with A/B testing, dataLayer analytics and a budget of under 8KB of JS per widget. No libraries, no jQuery, no React.
items.context: The store paid Rebuy to power product recommendations across the storefront. It came with third-party JavaScript weight, little control over UX and ranking logic, and a monthly bill. So I built the equivalent from scratch, with more flexibility, better performance and the experimentation layer under our own roof. It's finished and queued for A/B testing as soon as the Algolia search test wraps up.
items.actions: Designed and built one unified Shopify OS 2.0 section (reco-unified.liquid) that renders 7 widget types through section blocks: Recently Viewed, Best Sellers (global and by category), PDP native recommendations, PLP/Collection recommendations, Cart recommendations (deduplicated, excluding what's already in the cart), Account recommendations (customer-aware), and Custom Collection. Data comes from Shopify's native recommendations endpoint, best-seller collections, localStorage for recently viewed history (TTL 14 days, max 20 items, deduped by ID), and the Sections Rendering API for card hydration. reco.js is a plain UMD module under 8KB gzip per widget: IntersectionObserver for lazy loading and impression tracking, A/B bucketing kept in localStorage for 30 days, and full dataLayer events (reco_impression, reco_click, reco_add_to_cart) carrying widget_type, position and ab_variant. For performance: skeleton placeholders to prevent CLS, lazy image loading, aspect-ratio reserved containers, and SSR card rendering in Liquid with JS hydration islands only where they're needed. Quick Add is accessible, with spinner states, aria-label, keyboard navigation and a POST to /cart/add.js that emits its own event. Stock filtering runs at every data source, so an out-of-stock product never renders.
items.impact: Built and ready to go out. It replaces Rebuy across 5 page templates with 6 live widget types, holds under 8KB gzip of JS per widget, and ships zero third-party dependencies. The A/B infrastructure was in from day one: bucketing, event tracking and variant labels on every analytics event. It goes live against Rebuy once the Algolia experiment is done.
